research_question: What is the evidence-based, teachable theory of TYPOGRAPHY for UI/web design — type scale, hierarchy, weight, line-length (measure), line-height (leading), font pairing, alignment, letter-spacing, and readability — and what mechanically-checkable PASS/FAIL rules can an AI design-review agent apply to type rendered in a Next/Tailwind/Radix/shadcn page?
openai_instructions: Focus on deductive precision: derive the numeric craft constants (modular scale ratios 1.125-1.5; measure 45-75ch / ~66 ideal; body line-height 1.4-1.6; min readable body size ~16px on web; max ~2 typefaces; weight as a hierarchy lever). For each, state the perceptual/readability mechanism, the checkable assertion, and the computed-style proxy. Build the failure tree of bad type (too-long measure, tight leading, grey-on-color, too many fonts, justified rag). Cite Refactoring UI Designing Text + Butterick/typography readability research + Material/HIG type systems as principle sources.
claude_instructions: Verify the contrarian angle: which 'rules' are myths or context-dependent (the 45-75ch range vs single optimum; line-height varying with measure and size; system-font stacks vs custom fonts performance tradeoff). Cross-verify the contrast coupling (type is also an accessibility surface — min size, contrast). Find measurable proxies an agent can compute via getComputedStyle (font-size, line-height, max-width/ch, font-family count, font-weight steps).
search_strategy: optimal line length measure characters per line readability
line height leading body text web
minimum font size mobile readability accessibility
exclusion_criteria: print-only typography with no screen relevance

required_output_schema.per_finding_format: claim, evidence, confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), source URLs, counter-evidence

phases.name: Landscape
sub_questions: What are the established typographic craft dimensions (scale, hierarchy, measure, leading, pairing, alignment, tracking) and how do the authorities define each?
Which dimensions carry hierarchy and which carry readability?
phases.evidence_priorities: Refactoring UI Designing Text, typography-mistakes articles, Material/HIG type systems
phases.stop_condition: Complete when all craft dimensions are enumerated with sources

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: The numeric craft constants and how to build them with tokens
sub_questions: What are the defensible numeric ranges (scale ratio, measure ch, line-height, min size, weight steps, max font count) and the mechanism behind each?
What computed-style proxies make each checkable?
phases.evidence_priorities: modular scale math, measure research, leading-vs-measure coupling, type tokens
phases.stop_condition: Complete when the numeric constants + computed proxies are documented

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: What bad type looks like and how it reads
sub_questions: What are the named failures (long measure, tight/loose leading, too many fonts, grey-on-color, tiny mobile body, all-caps long runs, justified rag, faux-bold) and the user symptom of each?
How can a reviewer detect each from computed styles?
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 6+ failure modes with detection signals documented

phases.name: Contrarian
phases.objective: Which type rules are context-dependent or myths
sub_questions: Which common typographic rules are oversimplified, and what is the nuanced truth (measure range vs optimum, leading varies, custom vs system font performance)?
phases.evidence_priorities: empirical readability studies vs folk rules, performance/CLS tradeoff of webfonts
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive counter-arguments with evidence found
